correctness.rationale: For each unrooted edge split a+b=n, the probability its bridge is needed is (1−q^a)(1−q^b)=1−q^a−q^b+q^n (q=1−p), yielding exact U(p). After twice differentiating and dividing by q^{n−2}>0, H(q)=n(n−1)L−sum ℓ[a(a−1)q^{-b}+b(b−1)q^{-a}] is strictly increasing from −infinity to positive H(1)=2sum ℓab; unique zero gives convex-to-concave U. Bernoulli inequality at q0=(n−2)/n yields H(q0)<=0, strict for any nonpendant split. Such split exists iff nonstar under stated no degree-two hypothesis, proving pT<=2/n and sharp equality star. Jensen under environmental common random P then yields opposite signs on either side, while the standard rooted edge sum is concave. Independent exact survival-set quartet polynomial 6−4q−4q²−4q³+6q⁴ and q=1/3 value 112/27 corroborate; finite example not universal proof.
